why: record friction met during the backfills over common

ops.section: 2026-10-17 write schema: the narrative section mode does not name overview.md as a target
ops.body: OM-005 (in common). `ks write schema --row narrative --mode section` lists the narrative row's targets as domains, standards, architecture, testing, styling, workflows and team-home paths; `overview.md` is not among them. Both drafting units read that as a reason to doubt their overview change-sets. `ks write plan --at common` accepted every `section` op on `overview.md` under the narrative writer. Expected: the schema's target list to include `overview.md`, since the engine routes it there. Done instead: went by the plan output and applied the change-sets.

ops.section: 2026-10-17 tag-backfill brief: no answer for empty headings and link lists in an untagged document
ops.body: OM-005 (in common). Eight of ten tagging passes over common's tool nodes reported the same hole in `skills/tag-backfill/tagging-brief.md`. `inherits` is defined as the document's tags or an enclosing heading covering the section, and `no-good-match` requires a missing concept. A heading with no body of its own, or a Related section holding only links, inside a document that got no document tags, fits neither: passes split between `inherits` (against its definition) and `no-good-match` with invented suggestions ("links to related documents"), which then reach the gap list. The same passes split on sub-topics of a term the document carries (Indentation, Braces, Comments under a `code-style` document): the `inherits` rule and the "vocabulary too coarse" warning give opposite answers. The brief's Output section also says to append in batches, which does not fit one JSON object; the manager's note said to rewrite the whole object. Expected: the brief to name the empty-heading and link-list case, and to say which rule wins for sub-topics of a document term. Done instead: triaged every such gap to no new term by hand.
